outcome: Give development director / property operations head a governed method to improve overdue high-risk safety actions using work permits, zone sensors and training records, with final decisions…
overview: Construction Safety Permit Monitoring addresses source evidence is scattered across documents and transaction systems, leading to repeated checks and incomplete case files in construction and real estate operations. The first proof of value uses work permits, zone sensors and training records. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is overdue high-risk safety actions, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: work permits, zone sensors and training records; define overdue high-risk safety actions and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Development Director / Property Operations Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including run golden documents and exceptions against the system of record.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for overdue high-risk safety actions
